html:
SMTO-MEM-0020 — Document search data is being rebuilt

GUID: 2791b8da-b937-59ab-9de9-054d5a80a7d5
Slug: knowledge-index-rebuilding
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • SMTO found that search data for some documents was missing and has started rebuilding it from their saved copies. Searches of those documents won't work until it finishes.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Leave the documents as they are and wait a few minutes while SMTO rebuilds their search data. The rebuild uses the saved copies, so replacing or deleting documents now only restarts the work.
  2. Open Knowledge › Test retrieval, choose the conversation, and search for something those documents contain. When passages from those documents appear, the rebuild has finished.
  3. Ask your question in the conversation again. Searching only reads data, so it is safe to repeat once the rebuild is done.
  4. If you see "Search index restore failed" instead, follow that message's steps. That message means the rebuild itself failed and needs a Reindex.

What success looks like

  • Test retrieval returns passages from the affected documents.

If it still fails

  • If searches keep reporting a rebuild after about an hour, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the documents; they are needed to rebuild the search data.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Document search found the vector collection missing for one or more document generations (index_missing), queued restore jobs to re-index their saved passages, and returned index_rebuilding for this request.

What this means

  • New search data is still being prepared. The current retrieval request cannot use the unfinished version. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported index_rebuilding. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • Indexing completes and the source appears in retrieval results.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Check that the vector database is running and that the queued restore jobs (identities starting with restore:) reach ready in /api/agent/rag/jobs. Retry the search after they complete; a failed restore is reported as index_restore_failed.
  • Keep the source and watch its indexing progress in Knowledge. Search again after indexing reaches Ready.

Retry and execution caution

  • Indexing completes and the source appears in retrieval results.

How to verify the fix

  • Indexing completes and the source appears in retrieval results.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
